verses.1: David punished the people with whom he was together. He put thousands of officers over them, as well as thousands of other soldiers.
verses.2: David sent the three men in the hands of Joab, and the three men in the hands of Abishai son of Zeruiah. Joab was his brother. The three men were also in the hands of Itai Haggiti. The king said to the people, “Let us go too, I will go with you.”
verses.3: And the people said, “Do not go out, for if they do, they will not have hearts to listen to us. And if they die, their sons will still not have hearts to listen to us. As it is now, there are twelve thousand of us. Now, it’s better for us to be taken from the city to the wilderness.”
verses.4: And the king said to them, “What you choose as good will be done.” Then the king stood by the gate, and all the people went out to watch.
verses.5: The king commanded Yoab, Abishai, and Itai, saying, “Do not give the young man to Absalom.” All the people heard the king’s command regarding Absalom.
verses.6: And the people of Sodom went out to fight against Israel. The battle took place in the forest of Efrém.
verses.7: And the people of Israel were terrified there before the servants of David. The terror was so great that on that day, there were twelve thousand people who died.
verses.8: And there was a great battle there, spreading over the entire land. The forests became full of food for those who ate from it on that day.
verses.9: And Abshalom stood before David’s servants. Abshalom rode on the ark of God. The ark was placed under the wings of that great God. Abshalom strengthened his head, and he separated between heaven and earth. The ark passed through between them.
verses.10: And one man saw this, and he reported it to Joab. He said, “Look! I saw Abshalom hanging there.”
verses.11: And Joab said to the man who told him this: “Now, see! You have seen it with your own eyes. But why didn’t you take her there? Now, I will give you ten pieces of silver and a belt.”
verses.12: And the man said to Joab, “I am burdened with a thousand pieces of silver on my shoulders. I cannot go to the king’s son. For in our ears, the king has ordered that you, your father, and I should be kept safe from harm.”
verses.13: I have done what was wrong in my heart. Nothing can be separated from the king; you will stand before him.
verses.14: And Joab said, “No, I will not do that before you.” Then he took three sticks in his hands and inserted them into the heart of Abshalom. Thus, he killed him.
verses.15: And they brought twelve young men who carried the utensils of Yawub. They attacked Abshalom and killed him.
verses.16: And Joshua set up the camp. The people stopped their pursuit of Israel, because Joshua had defeated them.
verses.17: They took Absalom and threw him into the forest, at the great tree. They placed huge stones on top of him. All of Israel rushed to their tents.
verses.18: And Absalom took her and placed her in his life. She was the concubine of the king. He said, “I have no son through my wife.” So he named her after himself. He called her “Absalom’s hand.” This is how it continued until today.
verses.19: And Ahimelech son of Zadok said, “Come, O land, and help me against the king, for Jehovah has judged him in his own hands.”
verses.20: And Joab said to him, “There is no one in Sheerah today who can serve as a commander. But tomorrow, you will be able to serve as a commander. And today, you shall not serve as a commander, because the king has died.”
verses.21: And Joab said to Koushiy, “Go and tell the king about what you have seen.” Koushiy bowed down to Joab and ran away.
verses.22: And Ahimelech son of Zadok gathered his men together. He said to Joab, “Please let me also go with them.” But Joab replied, “Why do you want to go with them, my son? There is no one who can lead us in battle.”
verses.23: And there was a land. He said to it, “Go!” And it ran away along the path of the forest. It passed through the bushes.
verses.24: And David sat between the two gates. He walked towards the gate’s edge, towards the open space. He raised his eyes and saw that there was a man running alone.
verses.25: And the scribe called out and reported to the king. The king said, “Let him go alone.” Then he went away and ate.
verses.26: And the guard saw a man running away. He called out to the guard and said, “Look! There’s a man running away alone.” The king also said, “That’s just another liar.”
verses.27: And the prophet said, “I see that the first harvest is like the harvest of Ahimelech son of Zadok.” And the king said, “This is a good man; let there be a good wife for him.”
verses.28: And Ahimelech called out to King Solomon. He bowed down before the king, to his feet, and said, “Blessed be Jehovah your God, who has closed the mouths of those who had raised their hands against the king.”
verses.29: And King Shalom said to the young man, “Abshalom.” Abshalom replied, “I have seen this great man. He will send away the king’s servant Yoav and your servant as well. I didn’t know anything about it.”
verses.30: And the king said, “Stand in this manner.” So he stood as it was commanded.
verses.31: And behold, the captain came and said, “I will report to your lord, the king, that Jehovah has judged you today by all those who stand against you.”
verses.32: And the king said to the chief priests, “Let this young man be released.” But the chief priests said, “He will become a rival to the king and all those who have opposed him in the past.”
